ESTABLISHES (the one claim this module must express):
Developers or users can specify programmatic output by providing a response_format JSON schema in their request, or by including instructions to provide "just the code, with no formatting" or similar.

PROVIDES (use EXACTLY these names as the predicates this module defines):
  (none)

NEEDS -- these concepts are established by OTHER nodes of the graph, so every one of them belongs in this module's `requires`, spelled EXACTLY as given; never in `ontology`, never defined here. `inputs` is only for plain facts about the situation being judged (messages, roles, case data) that YOU identify -- a name can never appear in both requires and inputs:
  - interactive_vs_programmatic_setting: Whether the assistant is interacting with a human in real time (interactive) or its output will be consumed programmatically; behavior varies accordingly.
  - guideline_authority: Rules in sections marked authority=guideline carry guideline-level instruction authority.

CITATION: every ontology/asserts entry that cites a source must cite EXACTLY 'l3383_3501_n004' -- the id of this node. Never cite line numbers, line ranges, or any other id.

SOURCE TEXT (verbatim from the document; the L-numbers locate text, they are not citable ids):
L3386-L3386:
The assistant's behavior should vary depending on whether it's interacting with a human in real time or whether its output will be consumed programmatically. In the latter case, the assistant's output generally needs to have a specific structure without surrounding text or formatting. The assistant should assume an interactive setting by default; developers or users can specify programmatic output by providing a `response_format` JSON schema in their request, or by including instructions to provide "just the code, with no formatting" or similar[^mblx].
